facts.statement: The genus Batrachognathus was named in 1948 by the Russian paleontologist Anatoly Nicolaevich Ryabinin.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 1948 by the Russian paleontologist Anatoly Nicolaevich Ryabinin.

facts.statement: The genus name Batrachognathus means "frog jaw" and refers to the animal's short, wide head.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from Greek batrakhos, "frog" and gnathos, "jaw", in reference to the short wide head.

facts.statement: Batrachognathus was a small pterosaur with an estimated wingspan of 50 to 75 cm and a body mass of 40 grams, though specimens may not have been adults.
facts.quote: Batrachognathus was a small pterosaur, with a wingspan of 50 - 75 cm and body mass of 40 g, although the known specimens may not be adults.

facts.statement: Three fossils of Batrachognathus have been found in lacustrine sediment in the North-West Tien Shan foothills of the Karatau Mountains.
facts.quote: Three fossils have been found in a lacustrine sediment in the North-West Tien Shan foothills of the Karatau Mountains.

facts.statement: The skull of Batrachognathus is high, short, and broad, measuring 48 mm in length.
facts.quote: The skull of 48 mm (1.9 in) long is high, short and broad.

facts.statement: Batrachognathus possessed 22 or 24 recurved conical teeth in its upper jaws, forming a short and very wide mouth.
facts.quote: The upper jaws have in total 22 or 24 recurved conical teeth; with the lower jaws they make a short and very wide mouth.

facts.statement: Batrachognathus had an orbitoantorbital fenestra, a single opening combining the orbit and antorbital fenestra, similar to that found in monofenestratan pterosaurs.
facts.quote: The orbit and antorbital fenestra of the skull are combined into a single opening, an orbitoantorbital fenestra, similar to the nasoantorbital fenestra of monofenestratan pterosaurs.

facts.statement: While the holotype lacks a tail, an undescribed specimen shows that Batrachognathus had a comparatively long tail similar to the related genus Sinomacrops.
facts.quote: Although the holotype does not preserve the tail, an undescribed specimen preserves a comparatively long tail for an anurognathid, similar to the closely related Sinomacrops.

facts.statement: A 2021 phylogenetic analysis placed Batrachognathus within the subfamily Batrachognathinae as the sister taxon to the genus Sinomacrops.
facts.quote: In 2021, a phylogenetic analysis conducted by Xuefang Wei and colleagues recovered Batrachognathus within the subfamily Batrachognathinae, sister taxon to the genus Sinomacrops.

facts.statement: Batrachognathus lived during the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian to Kimmeridgian stages) in the Karabastau Formation of Kazakhstan.
facts.quote: Batrachognathus is an extinct genus of anurognathid pterosaur from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian to Kimmeridgian) Karabastau Formation of the central Asian republic of Kazakhstan.

facts.statement: Batrachognathus volans lived approximately 150 million years ago during the Oxfordian to Kimmeridgian stages in the Karabastau Svita region of Kazakhstan.
facts.quote: Batrachognathus volans es una especie extinta de pterosaurio ranforrincoideo de la familia Anurognathidae que vivió hace 150 million years ago, en las etapas del Oxfordiense al Kimmeridgiense en la región de Karabastau Svita en Kazajistán (Asia central).

facts.statement: Batrachognathus was assigned to the family Anurognathidae as a relative of Anurognathus.
facts.quote: El género Batrachognathus fue asignado a la familia Anurognathidae, como un pariente de Anurognathus.

facts.statement: In 2003, Alexander Kellner grouped Batrachognathus with the Asian anurognathids Dendrorhynchoides and Jeholopterus into the clade Asiaticognathidae.
facts.quote: En 2003 fue unido con los anurognátidos asiáticos Dendrorhynchoides y Jeholopterus en el clado Asiaticognathidae por Alexander Kellner.

facts.statement: The wingspan of Batrachognathus is estimated at about 50 cm, though David Unwin estimated it to be as large as 75 cm in 2000.
facts.quote: Se estima su envergadura en unos 50 centímetros, aunque David Unwin en 2000 dio una estimació mayor, de 75 centímetros.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Batrachognathus had a tail since it was not preserved in the holotype, but it is generally assumed to have had a short tail like other anurognathids.
facts.quote: La cola del animal no se preservó, por lo que sí tenía una es debatible; por lo general se asume que tenía una cola corta como otros anurognátidos.

facts.statement: Batrachognathus lived between 161.5 and 154.8 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Oxfordian (161.5 to 154.8 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Batrachognathus is assumed to have been an insectivore that caught insects and perhaps small fish on the wing using its broad mouth.
rejected.quote: Like all anurognathids Batrachognathus is assumed to have been an insectivore, catching insects and perhaps small fish on the wing with its broad mouth.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'insects and perhaps small fish on the wing'
